question: At fixed entrance, depth, initial order, stationary lattice registration and phase bias, does a single global winding balance radial shape work at an exit wide enough to drain through a dense subsonic annulus?
scope: Signed absolute material plus carrier radial work on the same held path. Finite resolved layer conditional on matched boundaries. No inference of globally relaxed support, absence of vortex shedding, or fracture threshold. Entrance radius 3 was not sampled.

controls.healing: Feasible positive changes of registered order on material and reconstructed carrier fields, with finite-difference check. Core density and lattice order measured separately.
controls.stress: Virtual work on signed exit widths measures net radial force. Integration of driven minus zero-drive normal stress measures axial transfer through a disk with a vortex present in both states.
controls.thresholds: Dense means at least half the unit bath density (strict inequality in resolved patch); normal and total speed compared separately to n^2.
controls.radius_one: Native mesh signs at .455 and .457. The weaker near-zero force at .455 is sensitive to refinement; .453 and .457 also bracket at standard resolution.
controls.admission: Five initial material entries and one subsequent order entry had no admitted child. All requested configurations were subsequently measured or independently available. No failed start is a force.
